title: Patch label data model and DSL nodes
description:
The label store from 'Labeling Mesh Patches': a tag set per patch plus a separate label hierarchy (parent -> children, PartNet/PartNeXt style), stored as a PatchLabels value class (public final fields, no records/nested classes) in a GeometryBundle slot whose name constant lives on PatchLabels. Patches are the layout's patches (patch_id IntField from PatchSurfaceGeometry); a face-level projection is derived, never stored twice. Nodes: `label_patches(geometry, label, parent="", points=[...])` -- selects patches by a surface point each (nearest face -> patch), obeying the geometric-selection ruling, and adds the label; `remove_label(geometry, label, points=[...])`; `label_to_selection(geometry, label)` -> per-face and per-vertex BoolField (the bridge into set_bone_weight, delete_geometry, set_label_material). Labels serialize as DSL statements appended to the saved layout .dsl from CRAW-4 (a PatchLabelsDslWriter), so a labeled model is one .dsl file.

SCOPE CHANGE (user, 2026-10-02): the saved layout is no longer CRAW-4's carrier-mesh .dsl. It is PATCH-57's self-contained Coons-patch .dsl, which needs no mesh file. Labels attach to PATCH-57's patches, and PatchLabelsDslWriter appends to that file. Read every mention of "the saved layout .dsl from CRAW-4" above as PATCH-57's .dsl.

SCOPE CHANGE (user, 2026-10-03): this becomes the one shared store for labels and groups on any mesh domain, not a patch-only store. The user wants arbitrary labelling, vertex groups and the like on faces, vertices (and edges) that save with the model, and wants ring regions (the segmentation of the crawfish scans into parts) and quad-layout patches to use the same system. So: (1) storage sits on MESH-23's named per-domain attributes (only its storage core is needed here, not its ten attribute nodes): a label or group is a named attribute on a domain, membership BoolField or id IntField, with the parent -> children label hierarchy kept alongside; (2) authoring and saving stay geometric per the original design: label statements select elements by surface points (a point picks a face, a ring region or a patch) and are appended to the model's .dsl, re-derived on load so they survive remeshing and ring edits; (3) consumers: ring regions first (label a region by a point inside it), PATCH-57 patches later through the same nodes; label_to_selection gives per-face and per-vertex selections for delete_geometry, set_bone_weight and materials; (4) fold tag_geometry's _tags per-vertex masks into it rather than keeping a second mechanism. PatchLabels becomes the generic label store; rename accordingly.
definition-of-done: 1. PatchLabels value + slot constant; multiple labels per patch; hierarchy queries (children, ancestors, all patches under a label). 2. Three nodes registered and documented; catalog regenerated; CanonicalPortNames allowlist updated if needed. 3. label_to_selection output drives set_bone_weight in a test graph on the plane fixture. 4. PatchLabelsDslWriter appends label statements to a saved layout and re-execution restores identical labels. 5. Unit tests on the plane-layout fixture only. 6. Build checkstyle-green.
testing-plan: 1. Unit: label two patches of plane_layout as 'top' under parent 'hand'; assert membership, hierarchy, and face projection. 2. Unit: label_to_selection -> set_bone_weight yields weight 1.0 exactly on the labelled patches' vertices. 3. Unit: writer round trip -- save, re-execute, compare PatchLabels equality. 4. ValidateDsl on the produced .dsl passes.
todos: Design PatchLabels (tag set per patch, hierarchy map) with slot constant
Nearest-face-to-point patch selection helper (reuse nearest_vertex machinery)
Unit tests on plane fixture; catalog regeneration
unknowns: Whether labels should attach to patch ids or to patch centroids so they survive a re-layout with a different id order (the .arr disease)
Whether the hierarchy belongs in the bundle slot or in a separate ontology .dsl shared across models
How a label on a patch that later gets split (boolean dirty marking, CRAW-15) should propagate
